claims.text: The untreated (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy has a coarse-grained microstructure.
The untreated alloy is inherently brittle and tends to crack during field- and pressure-driven caloric cycling.
ECAP will refine the grains of (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38.
ECAP will produce a more uniform grain structure.
ECAP will reduce concentrations of stress-inducing defects.
ECAP will reduce large-grain regions that act as crack-initiation sites.
Severe plastic deformation and grain refinement will disperse residual stresses.
Severe plastic deformation and grain refinement will reduce the size and frequency of microstructural flaws.
Dispersing residual stresses and reducing microstructural flaws will enhance toughness.
The phase transformation responsible for the caloric effect depends on chemical composition and intrinsic structural changes rather than absolute grain size.
Consequently, ECAP-induced grain refinement will leave caloric performance essentially unaltered.
ECAP-treated samples will have greater fracture toughness than untreated samples.
ECAP-treated samples will have lower crack density than untreated samples.
The adiabatic temperature change and entropy change of ECAP-treated samples will remain within approximately 10% of the untreated alloy's values.
The untreated alloy exhibits a large caloric response under applied magnetic and pressure fields.
The intervention is applicable near the phase-transformation temperature under the magnetic and pressure fields used for refrigeration.
Severe plastic deformation may alter phase-transformation kinetics or hysteresis.
Any caloric changes caused by altered transformation kinetics or hysteresis are expected to remain within approximately 10%.
